page_note: Heavily hortatory page. The Teacher addresses the audience ('you') with pastoral instruction: how to react when others become wroth, the silent forbearance of the holy ones, recognition of the two substances dwelling in every man. No cosmic mapping, no zoomorphic correspondence, no enumeration. Even the doctrinal references ('mystery of the two substances') are framed as recapitulation ('since you have known...') rather than substrate exposition. Teaching purity 0.0 and dominant hortatory vocabulary throughout. The 'two substances' allusion is reflective of substrate doctrine but rhetorically deployed for ethical exhortation about not despising fellow Manichaeans who fall into anger or sin.

'They have done the purpose-of-heart of the Greatness'—still describing audience behavior, leads into pastoral exhortation.
'ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ' (Again) connector introducing description of times of disturbance—setup for the pastoral instruction that follows.
Direct prohibition: 'but you, do not be disturbed in your...' — explicit hortatory voice with ⲙⲡⲱⲣ. Score 71.43.
'knowing rather that they stand fast in a body...' — pastoral didactic continuation.

'kneaded into the flesh of Sin which also dwells in a strange land' — uses cosmic vocabulary (Sin, strange land) but as pastoral explanation of why fellow believers grow angry, not as substrate mapping.
Continuation of the explanation of why people become wroth — pastoral causation.
'speak and proclaim hard words' — pastoral description of behavior to be tolerated.

'nor set yourself up against them, do not say...' — chain of prohibitions. Score 125.0.

'Since you have known the mystery of the two substances'—doctrinal recap framed as pastoral premise; not substrate teaching but reference to it. The score flagged ⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ as ecclesial, but the function here is hortatory recapitulation.

'you have learned also that the holy ones bear under a great burden' — pastoral characterization of the Elect, not cosmic substrate.

'since you yourself also have known that they bear up under...' — repetition of pastoral premise.
'a great burden, they stand fast in the body which is not theirs' — continued characterization of the Elect.

'sins, the holy ones are filled (with grief) on your account' — pastoral characterization.
